title: Engineering Intrinsic Mixed Sodium Ionic–Electronic Conductivity in a Nickel Bis(diimine) Metal–Organic Framework
abstract: Abstract Mixed ionic–electronic conductors (MIECs) are highly desirable for a wide range of electronic applications, however, developing single-phase MIECs with intrinsic transport properties under ambient conditions remains challenging. Herein, we report a Na+-ion and electron mixed-conducting metal–organic framework (MOF), Ni-HITP-SO3Na, by tethering anionic sulfonate side chains with Na+ counterions onto the 2,3,6,7,10,11-hexaiminotriphenylene (HITP) ligand of a d-π conjugated nickel bis(diimine)-based framework. Ni-HITP-SO3Na is highly crystalline with honeycomb networks and microporous with surface area of 412 m2 g–1. Remarkably, Ni-HITP-SO3Na exhibits dual transport without relying on conductive fillers, guest electrolytes, or external ion sources. Four-probe measurements reveal a high electronic conductivity of 0.7 ± 0.3 S cm–1, and DC polarization yields a sodium ionic conductivity of (3.7 ± 0.7) × 10–6 S cm–1 at room temperature in the solid state, which can be further improved to (1.5 ± 0.4) × 10–5 S cm–1 with the assistance of solvents. These results, to the best of our knowledge, demonstrate the first MOF that intrinsically combines electronic and sodium ionic conduction, delivering competitive mixed conductivity among reported MIECs, particularly under ambient temperature. The mixed conductivity originates from the intact d–π conjugation for electronic transport and the sulfonate-functionalized pore walls that afford low-barrier Na+ pathways via a relay transport mechanism involving transient bridging coordination between neighboring sulfonate groups. This work highlights embedding ion-transport functionality directly into conductive MOF backbones as an effective route to structurally well-defined, highly porous framework MIECs for electrochemical and iontronic devices.

title: Tetrapyridophenazine-Based Vinylene-Linked Covalent Organic Frameworks for Efficient Sequential Photocatalysis and Continuous-Flow Synthesis
abstract: Abstract Vinylene-linked covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are promising photocatalysts because their conjugated sp2-carbon frameworks combine exceptional chemical stability with efficient charge transport. However, the limited reversibility of C═C bond formation narrows the scope of polymerizable monomers, restricting the structural diversity and electronic tunability of vinylene-linked COFs. Here, we report a molecular design strategy based on a planar, electron-deficient, nitrogen-rich tetrapyridophenazine (TTPhz) building block for constructing vinylene-linked COFs. Knoevenagel polycondensation of a polymerizable TTPhz monomer with aromatic dialdehydes affords three highly crystalline COFs with tunable donor–acceptor interactions and electronic structures. The optimized fluorinated framework, TTPhz-COF-3, exhibits efficient charge separation and transport, enabling a previously unreported one-pot sequential photocatalytic synthesis of 2,3-dihydrobenzofuran derivatives from arylboronic acids through tandem aerobic hydroxylation and oxidative [3 + 2] cycloaddition. The catalyst displays broad substrate scope, excellent recyclability, and enables gram-scale continuous-flow synthesis of a key intermediate of the natural product (±)-conocarpan with a 4-fold higher turnover frequency than the corresponding batch process. This work expands the structural and functional scope of vinylene-linked COFs and establishes molecular building-block design as a general strategy for developing advanced crystalline organic photocatalysts.

title: Charge Donated by the Framework, Reactivity Expressed at the Metal: Tetrathiafulvalene-Programmed Nitrate Reduction to Ammonia
abstract: The decisive challenge in nitrate-to-ammonia electrosynthesis is not simply supplying electrons, but ensuring that successive nitrogen intermediates remain chemically convertible. Here, we establish a molecular strategy that differentiates framework-derived electronic character from metal-directed reaction selectivity through TU-420, a crystalline covalent organic framework integrating electron-donating tetrathiafulvalene and electron-accepting, metal-coordinating bipyridine units. Electronic-structure analysis identifies complementary donor-associated and acceptor-like states, while Xray absorption spectroscopy reveals distinct approximately six-coordinate Fe–O/N and four-coordinate Cu–O/N environments within the conserved architecture. Remarkably, TU-420-Fe achieves 98.1% ammonia Faradaic efficiency at −0.60 V versus the reversible hydrogen electrode and an ammonia production rate of 4.33 mg h-1 cm-2 at −0.80 V, whereas TU-420-Cu exhibits substantially lower selectivity despite its stronger cathodic response. Isotope-labeling experiments establish nitrate as the nitrogen source, while in situ attenuated total reflectance surface-enhanced infrared absorption spectroscopy, Raman spectroscopy, and differential electrochemical mass spectrometry reveal signatures consistent with evolving nitrogen–oxygen and hydrogenated nitrogen species. Density functional theory identifies the mechanistic distinction: Fe supports a favorable *NHO-mediated reduction sequence with a maximum uphill free-energy increment of 0.30 eV, while substantially alleviating the energetic penalty associated with the competing *NOH-mediated route relative to Cu. These findings identify the energetic fate of partially reduced nitrogen, rather than electron consumption alone, as a determinant of ammonia selectivity and establish electronically differentiated covalent architectures as platforms for programming metal-dependent multielectron catalysis.

title: Reimpregnation of Disordered Mesopores by Ionic Liquids
abstract: Abstract The reimpregnation, i.e., replacement of the soft-templating ionic liquid (IL, BMIM-TFSI) that forms the porosity during the synthesis of disordered mesoporous silica-based (ionosilica) materials, has been studied by an original combination of small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS), thermogravimetric analysis, and nitrogen sorption. The architecture of the mesoporous scaffold was identified by SAXS after IL extraction using ethanol. Subsequently, the same ionic liquid, or IL-ethanol mixtures, were reintroduced into the ionosilica after a vacuum treatment, allowing controlled IL filling up to total reimpregnation of the mesopores. By confronting SAXS, where the intensity is a direct function of the degree of filling, with BET giving access to filling-dependent mesopore surface areas, a striking convergence of results shows that macroscopic and microscopic techniques target the same physical characteristics. In particular, the mesopores are shown to fill in a controlled way, one after the other, up to high degrees of filling.

title: Stereoselective polysubstituted bicyclo[1.1.0]butane synthesis by rhodium-catalyzed kinetic resolution
abstract: Bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes (BCBs) are a distinctive class of strained small-ring carbocycles of growing importance in synthetic and medicinal chemistry. However, the enantioselective synthesis of polysubstituted BCBs remains a largely unsolved challenge. In this study, we report a general chemical platform for the stereoselective assembly of chiral or meso 1,2,3,4-tetrasubstituted BCBs from internal alkynes and carbenes through stepwise [2+1+1’] or one-pot [2+1+1] cycloaddition reactions, respectively. Successful execution of these transformations exploits the combination of triftosylhydrazones (carbene precursors) and chiral dirhodium catalysts. The sterically hindered catalyst Rh 2 ( R -3,5- di PheTPCP) 4 features a confined chiral microenvironment that enables exquisite discrimination between cyclopropene enantiomers, affording highly enantioenriched polysubstituted BCBs through kinetic resolution upon reaction with chiral rhodium carbenes. This chemistry operates under mild reaction conditions, uses readily available starting materials, and exhibits broad substrate scope.

title: Structural basis for size-selective perception of chitin in plants
abstract: Plants detect microbes through pattern recognition receptors that perceive conserved microbial surface motifs known as microbe-associated molecular patterns (MAMPs). Lysin motif (LysM) receptors recognize and mediate downstream responses to chitinous MAMPs. In this study, we elucidated the mechanism for the specific recognition of long-chain chitin oligomers and identified a hallmark bridge domain characteristic of the CHITIN PERCEPTION (CHIP) receptor class. Structural analysis of receptor-ligand complexes, biochemistry, and in planta functional studies of inhibitory nanobodies revealed the mechanism of size-selective, high-affinity chitin perception in Lotus japonicus and Medicago truncatula . Additionally, we identified the CHITIN ELICITOR RECEPTOR KINASE (CERK) class as low-affinity, yet essential, co-receptors and propose a mechanistic model for a ligand-induced core signaling heterocomplex. Our findings establish the structural and mechanistic basis of differential chitin perception and receptor complex assembly in chitin-elicited plant immune signaling.

title: Boundary Guided Liquid‐Bridge Adhesion for Robotic Pick‐and‐Release
abstract: ABSTRACT Liquid‐bridge‐mediated adhesion provides conformal contact with rough surfaces and gentle interaction with fragile microstructures, making it attractive for object manipulation. However, controlling liquid‐bridge formation and retraction under non‐ideal interfacial conditions remains challenging. Here, we report a switchable liquid‐bridge adhesion strategy using a two‐tiered stamp with spatially patterned wettability. Boundary‐guided pinning confines liquid spreading to form a stable bridge for pickup and guides liquid retraction toward bridge breakup for controlled release. This design converts liquid‐bridge adhesion from an uncontrolled capillary phenomenon into a controllable interfacial mechanism. The strategy enables preload‐free adhesion switching, tunable adhesion forces, robust manipulation across surfaces with diverse roughness and wettability, and damage‐free contact with fragile microstructures. Integrated with a robotic platform, the stamp functions as a liquid‐bridge‐based robotic end effector for pick‐and‐place manipulation and robotic placement, providing a route toward ultra‐gentle manufacturing and microelectronic assembly.

title: Beyond Facet Engineering: Dislocation‐Mediated Nucleation Enables Stable Lithium Deposition on Practical Polycrystalline Cu Collectors
abstract: ABSTRACT Uniform Li deposition on practical Cu current collectors remains challenging in lithium metal batteries. Despite extensive efforts in facet engineering, achieving homogeneous Li deposition on practical polycrystalline Cu collectors remains elusive, highlighting an incomplete understanding of the structural factors governing Li deposition. Herein, a defect‐mediated interfacial engineering strategy is developed by simultaneously introducing a high density of geometrically necessary dislocations (GNDs) and enriched <110>/<111> textures on commercial electrodeposited Cu foils. Theoretical calculations and experiments reveal that densely distributed dislocations provide thermodynamically favorable Li adsorption sites and abundant preferential heterogeneous nucleation sites, while the enriched <110>/<111> textures promote Li surface diffusion and lateral growth. This combined effect promotes uniform and compact initial Li deposition, guiding path‐dependent deposition evolution and suppressing interfacial heterogeneity. The control experiments further support a key contribution of dislocation defects, while variations in surface chemistry or morphology alone cannot account for the observed performance differences. The optimized Cu foil sustains over 1200 cycles with an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.52% ± 0.20% over the final 200 cycles ( n = 4) in Li||Cu cells and improves N/P = 0 Cu||NCM811 full‐cell cycling. This work establishes dislocation‐mediated nucleation and orientation‐regulated growth as a design principle for practical Cu current collectors.

title: Hierarchical Ion-Conducting Materials Based on Polymer-Aligned Nanoparticles within Poly(vinyl benzyl methoxy poly(ethylene oxide) ether)- block -polystyrene Diblock Copolymer
abstract: Abstract Solid polymer electrolytes based on poly(ethylene oxide) (PEO) are promising alternatives to liquid electrolytes for safer lithium-ion batteries. Here, we report hierarchical solid polymer electrolytes obtained by selectively incorporating lithium sulfonamide-functionalized polymer nanoparticles (LiNPs) into a microphase-separated poly(vinyl benzyl methoxy poly(ethylene oxide) ether)-block-polystyrene block copolymer. Transmission electron microscopy (TEM), atomic force microscopy (AFM), and small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) demonstrate that the phase-segregated lamellar morphology of the block copolymer is preserved upon nanoparticle incorporation. Notably, the LiNPs preferentially localize within the poly(ethylene glycol)-rich lamellae, generating hierarchical structures with ordering across multiple length scales arising from block copolymer self-assembly, selective nanoparticle organization, and poly(ethylene glycol) crystallization. Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) reveals that the crystallinity of the poly(ethylene glycol) phase depends strongly on nanoparticle loading and plasticizer content. These hierarchical electrolytes exhibit high ionic conductivity, which is further enhanced by the addition of sulfolane as a plasticizer. These results elucidate the interplay between hierarchical morphology, phase crystallinity, and ion transport in block copolymer-based solid electrolytes, providing design guidelines for mechanically robust solid electrolytes with enhanced transport performance.

title: Disentangling Modulator and Fluoride Chemistry in Rare-Earth Metal–Organic Framework Formation via Multinuclear NMR Spectroscopy: A Mechanism-Guided Synthetic Redesign
abstract: Abstract Metal–organic framework (MOF) chemistry continues to expand, highlighting the need for molecular insight into framework formation. Solution-phase NMR provides a powerful, accessible, and economical means to probe these mechanisms. We examine the formation of rare-earth (RE) UiO-66, focusing on Yttrium(III)-UiO-66. RE-UiO-66 contains a hexa-metallic node in which the metals are bridged by μ3-fluorido, μ3-hydroxido, and/or μ3-oxido ligands, with benzenedicarboxylate linkers connecting nodes. The fluorido ligand derives from the α-fluorinated modulators required for this synthesis, yet its formation and incorporation pathways are unclear. Using in situ multinuclear NMR spectroscopy, we demonstrate that MOF formation proceeds via zero-order kinetics. Modulator is consumed approximately an order of magnitude faster than linker. The fluoride ligand is formed via nucleophilic aromatic substitution between modulator and in situ-generated dimethylamine. Mass balance suggests that the modulator plays a dual role, coordinating to the metal cation and generating fluoride. However, when solvent hydrolysis precedes MOF formation, the modulator acts primarily as a fluoride source; in situ-formed acetic acid acts as the modulator. Thus, the dual modulator role can be decoupled; benzoic acid functions as the modulator and tetramethylammonium fluoride serves as the fluoride source. Under these modified conditions, linker consumption is slow. When solvent hydrolysis precedes MOF formation, the reaction accelerates. This highlights the complex influence of acidity, competitive binding of fluoride, modulator, and linker on kinetically labile rare-earth metals. The tetramethylammonium fluoride procedure provides a versatile pathway to RE-UiO-66 derivatives (RE = Eu, Gd, Tb, Dy, Ho, Er, Yb, Lu) and two Y-UiO-67 derivatives.

title: Photocatalytic Tandem Reaction for Urea Synthesis From Atmospheric CO 2 and N 2
abstract: ABSTRACT Photocatalytic urea synthesis directly from atmospheric CO 2 and N 2 offers a sustainable route to bypass the energy‐intensive Bosch–Meiser process, yet simultaneously achieving CO 2 capture and reduction, N 2 activation, and C─N coupling within a single system remains challenging. Herein, we report a two‐step tandem platform combining ionic‐liquid‐modified metal–organic framework (IL@PCN‐250‐Fe 2 Co) with a trinuclear copper‐based covalent organic framework (HTP‐Cu 3 ‐imi‐COF) for urea photosynthesis from air. The IL@MOF captures atmospheric CO 2 and photoreduces it to CO, while HTP‐Cu 3 ‐imi‐COF couples the generated CO with ambient N 2 into urea. This synergistic tandem configuration delivers a urea production rate of 259.87 µg·g cat −1 ·h −1 under air, marking the first demonstration of photocatalytic urea synthesis from atmospheric CO 2 and N 2 . In situ spectroscopic measurements and DFT calculations reveal that the imidazole‐functionalized HTP segments act as hole‐rich oxidation domains, promoting water oxidation to generate *OH species that oxidize locally enriched N 2 to *NO intermediates. Simultaneously, the Cu 3 clusters serve as electron‐rich centers for CO adsorption and activation, forming *CO that couples with *NO via the critical *OCNO intermediate toward urea formation. This work not only showcases the first photocatalytic urea synthesis from air but also establishes a modular paradigm for cascade catalysts that integrate capture and conversion toward sustainable chemical transformations.

title: From Dark Photocatalysis to Photobattery‐Type Operation: A Re‐Functionalized Ti‐MOF for Solar Energy Storage
abstract: ABSTRACT Efficient harvesting, storage, and on‐demand release of solar energy are essential for overcoming the intermittency of sunlight and enabling continuous solar energy‐driven processes, yet achieving storage of photogenerated charge remains challenging. Here, we report a Ti‐based bipyridine MOF, COK47‐bpy, and its ReCl(CO) 3 ‐functionalized analogue, ReCl47‐bpy , as photochargeable materials for time‐decoupled solar energy utilization. Re incorporation introduces localized photosensitizing and “electron sink” sites while preserving the parent framework structure, enabling visible‐light response, faster charge accumulation, and improved charge retention. In colloidal suspension, ReCl47‐bpy reaches an electron storage capacity of 19.5 C g −1 MOF under simulated solar irradiation and retains about 70% of the stored charge after 2.5 months. The stored electrons can be released on demand for dark hydrogen (H 2 ) evolution with electron‐to‐H 2 efficiencies exceeding 90%. Beyond colloids, when fabricated as robust FTO‐supported layers, ReCl47‐bpy |FTO photoelectrodes deliver capacities of up to ∼7.0 mAh g −1 MOF upon photocharging under 1 Sun irradiation. Overall, this work establishes Re‐functionalized Ti‐MOFs as versatile platforms for solar‐driven charge storage, dark photocatalysis, and MOF‐based photoelectrodes, toward the development of next‐generation MOF‐based energy devices.

title: Layered Spin‐Crossover Metal‐Organic Frameworks for Light‐Induced Control of Two‐Dimensional Quantum Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Metal‐organic frameworks (MOFs) are widely explored for gas separation, catalysis, or energy storage, yet their integration with other electronically functional materials remains largely unexplored. Here, we integrate the layered Hofmann‐type spin‐crossover (SCO) MOF {Fe II (pyS 2 Et) 2 [Pt II (CN) 4 ]} into electrical nanodevices to control the properties of two‐dimensional (2D) quantum materials. Our molecular approach exploits the stimuli‐responsive nature of SCO‐layered materials as switchable building blocks. We demonstrate selective modulation of the electronic transport in van der Waals heterostructures interfacing SCO with 2D quantum materials (few‐layer graphene, magnetic CrSBr, superconducting NbSe 2 ) through the strain induced via thermal and light‐induced spin transitions. In graphene, the conductivity is selectively switched by light. In spin‐valves based on CrSBr bilayers, the MOF triggers magnetic hysteresis (absent in pristine CrSBr) and enables tunable non‐volatile zero‐field memory. In NbSe 2 , light modulates the superconducting critical current and transition temperature. These results establish layered stimuli‐responsive SCO MOFs as active molecular control elements for 2D quantum materials, providing a route to strain‐mediated control of electronic, magnetic, and superconducting functionalities, and extending MOF‐based architectures beyond traditional porous‐matter applications toward multifunctional electronics and spintronics.

title: Bioinspired Adaptive Ångström‐Channels in a Hydrogen‐Bonded Metal–Organic Framework for Selective Water Removal From Gas Streams by Molecular Sieving Dehydration
abstract: ABSTRACT The removal of water from light hydrocarbons is a critical yet energy‐intensive step in petrochemical processes. Conventional adsorbents often suffer from high regeneration temperatures and undesirable co‐adsorption. Inspired by the selective water transport mechanism of aquaporins, we report a hydrogen‐bonded metal–organic framework, ZNU‐33, featuring bioinspired adaptive one‐dimensional channels. The pore walls are decorated with both positively charged (Hbpa + ) and negatively charged (HEDP 4− ) recognition sites. Using in situ single‐crystal x‐ray diffraction, we captured five phases of ZNU‐33, activated (ZNU‐33‐α), intermediate (ZNU‐33‐β), partially dehydrated (ZNU‐33‐γ and ZNU‐33‐γ2), and fully hydrated ZNU‐33, directly visualizing a water‑triggered structural transition. Structural snapshots reveal water uptake proceeding from free‐channel water to Cu 2+ coordination and then to extended hydrogen‐bonded water chains. ZNU‐33 exhibits high water uptake (9.50 mmol/g at 2.85 kPa and 298 K) and negligible adsorption of CO 2 and all light hydrocarbons. Breakthrough experiments demonstrate efficient water removal under wide flow rates, temperatures, and humidity levels, with water‐adsorption capacity recoverable under substantially milder activation conditions than those required by the investigated conventional zeolites. This work not only provides a high‑performance material for selective dehydration, but also establishes a bioinspired adaptive adsorption mechanism for designing water‐selective adsorbents.

title: Unilateral Functionalization of Covalent Organic Frameworks: Local Electronic Modulation and Morphology-Enabled Mass Transport for Electrocatalytic Hydrogen Peroxide Production
abstract: Abstract Achieving high selectivity and activity in the two-electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e– ORR) pathway critically depends on the synergistic modulation of a catalyst’s electronic structure and mass diffusion channels. This work proposes an asymmetric modulation strategy via unilateral functionalization, in which −CH3, −CN, −SO3H, and −NO2 moieties are incorporated into a series of covalent organic frameworks (COFs), systematically unraveling the multilevel regulatory mechanisms exerted by functional groups from molecular to macroscopic morphological scales. The research demonstrates that introducing strong electron-withdrawing −NO2 groups can effectively enhance charge transfer at adjacent carbon active sites, reduce the formation barrier of OOH* intermediates, and induce efficient 2e– ORR activity. Concurrently, the polarity and steric effects of functional groups induce structural evolution in COFs from spherical, rod-like to spiderweb-like architectures, wherein the interconnected network of COF-NO2 substantially enhances the diffusion efficiency of reactants and products. This synergy between electronic structure and macroscopic morphology enables COF-NO2 to achieve 94% H2O2 selectivity and a high production rate of 10.5 mol gcat–1 h–1 with sustained stability. This work not only provides outstanding catalysts for efficient electrochemical H2O2 synthesis but also clarifies functional group-induced electronic and morphological modulation, offering a novel paradigm for the rational design of porous catalytic materials.

title: From α-Helices to Mesoscale Order: Structure–Packing Relationships in Polypeptide Block Copolymer Films
abstract: Abstract Polypeptide-based block copolymers are promising platforms for creating hierarchical nanostructures because their secondary structures can direct mesoscale self-assembly. This study investigates how polypeptide chain length and thermal annealing govern the hierarchical organization of poly(ethylene glycol)-b-poly(ε-benzyloxycarbonyl-l-lysine) (PEG-b-PZLL) thin films. Combined FTIR, AFM, AFM-IR, and synchrotron GIWAXS/GISAXS analyses reveal that PZLL segments predominantly form α-helical conformations that assemble into hexagonally packed domains with nearly constant lattice parameters across compositions. Increasing the PZLL degree of polymerization stabilizes the α-helical structure, promotes preferential in-plane orientation of cylindrical domains, and enables the formation of long-range ordered fibrillar morphologies, whereas short PZLL chains partially transform into β-sheet structures during film formation and after high-temperature annealing. These findings establish a direct relationship between the secondary structure, orientational ordering, and mesoscale morphology in self-assembled polypeptide block copolymer films.

title: Chiralizing Covalent Organic Frameworks to Boost H 2 O 2 Photosynthesis
abstract: ABSTRACT Solar‐driven H 2 O 2 photosynthesis offers a sustainable route to on‐site oxidant production, yet the selective reduction of triplet O 2 to spin‐paired H 2 O 2 remains kinetically challenging. Covalent organic framework (COF) photocatalysts have largely focused on charge separation and active‐site reactivity, while overlooking the spin character of electrons transferred to O 2 . Here we discover that chiralization renders COFs significantly enhanced production of H 2 O 2 , and report a chiralization strategy for spin‐regulated H 2 O 2 photosynthesis in β‐ketoenamine‐linked COFs. The chiral frameworks enable spin‐selective electron transport, favor the O–O‐bond‐preserving reduction pathway and lower the apparent kinetic barrier for H 2 O 2 formation. Chiralization enhances H 2 O 2 production by 38.7%–252.1% relative to achiral counterparts. A bipyridine‐containing chiral COF reaches 22.8 mmol g −1 h −1 using solely water and oxygen, with an apparent quantum yield of 10.3% at 420 nm, placing it at the forefront of sacrificial‐agent‐free COF systems. Membrane‐integrated chiral COFs enable continuous‐flow H 2 O 2 production. These findings establish chirality as a design parameter coupling spin‐selective electron transport with O 2 reduction pathway control, opening new directions for COF photocatalysis.

title: MnO₂ NANOCOMPOSITES ELECTRODE MATERIAL FOR SUPERCAPACITOR: A REVIEW OF LITERATURE
abstract: Supercapacitors are promising electrochemical energy-storage devices because of their high power density, rapid charge–discharge capability, and long cycle life. Among various electrode materials, manganese dioxide MnO₂ has attracted considerable attention due to its low cost, natural abundance, environmental compatibility, and high theoretical specific capacitance. However, the practical application of pristine MnO₂ is limited by its relatively low electrical conductivity, incomplete utilization of active material, and structural degradation during repeated charge–discharge cycles. Nanocomposite engineering has therefore emerged as an effective strategy to overcome these limitations by combining MnO₂ with conductive and structurally stable materials. This review presents a comprehensive overview of recent literature on MnO₂-based nanocomposite electrode materials for supercapacitor applications. Particular attention is given to MnO₂ composites incorporating carbon-based materials, conductive polymers, and other metal oxides, along with the influence of morphology, particle size, porosity, crystallinity, and interfacial structure on electrochemical performance. The review also discusses important synthesis approaches, including hydrothermal, sol–gel, electrodeposition, precipitation, and microwaveassisted methods. These strategies can improve electrical conductivity, ion diffusion, active surface area, rate capability, and cycling stability. Literature indicates that the formation of hierarchical and porous nanocomposite architectures provides synergistic effects between MnO₂ and its supporting materials, resulting in enhanced charge-storage performance. Overall, MnO₂ nanocomposites represent a promising pathway toward high-performance and sustainable supercapacitor electrodes, although challenges related to scalable synthesis, long-term stability, and practical device-level performance remain to be addressed.

title: Confined‐Space Self‐Assembly of Nano‐HNS Into Hierarchical Micro‐Nano Structured Microspheres for Selective Stimuli Sensitization and Passivation
abstract: To address the balance between reactivity and safety in nano-HNS, this study presents a green composite molding strategy that facilitates the self-assembly of nano-HNS into micro-nano-structured microspheres within confined spaces. This approach utilizes confined spaces to precisely control the morphology and size of the resultant microspheres. The effects of process parameters on the morphology and size of microspheres were systematically investigated, and the underlying formation mechanisms were elucidated. Comprehensive characterizations encompassing morphology, crystal structure, mechanical sensitivity, thermal behavior, and impact properties were conducted. The results demonstrate that the synthesized HNS microspheres possess high sphericity, an average particle size of 224.2 µm, and exhibit favorable fluidity and bulk density. This approach effectively reduces the mechanical sensitivity of the material while preserving the crystal structure and thermal stability of HNS-IV (impact sensitivity: 12 J vs. 20 J; friction sensitivity: 216 N vs. 240 N). Furthermore, it enhances the initial sensitivity to short duration shock, as evidenced by reductions in the 50% and 99.9% initiation voltages by 18 and 48 V, respectively. This approach facilitates the synergistic stimulation of selective sensitization and passivation. This methodology is straightforward and applicable, providing a versatile and eco-friendly approach for the multi-structural modification of nano-HNS.

title: Compartmentalized Dynamic Supramolecular Hydrogels through Chemically Fueled Self‐Assembly in Aqueous Two‐Phase Systems
abstract: ABSTRACT Compartmentalized dynamic supramolecular structures are prevalent in living systems and underpin numerous pivotal biological functions, yet their recapitulation in synthetic scenarios remains largely underexplored. Here, we report on compartmentalized supramolecular hydrogels that can dynamically evolve their structure and properties through chemically fueled self‐assembly in aqueous two‐phase systems (ATPSs) and uncover an unexpected dynamic interactive behavior between the hydrogel networks and ATPSs. By chemically fueling the self‐assembly of a simple peptide‐based gelator throughout aqueous emulsions of two immiscible polymer solutions, compartmentalized supramolecular hydrogel networks are generated. With the fuel dissipation, these hydrogels spontaneously disintegrate over time, with tunable lifetime and regeneration capacity. Interestingly, during the fueling process, the gelators are covalently decorated by one of the polymers in the ATPS, imparting the resultant hydrogel network with homotypic affinity for the corresponding polymer phase. This affinity drives an unexpected migration of the polymer phase, reminiscent of the migration of living cells assisted by the extracellular matrix. In turn, we leverage the polymer‐decorated gelator to control the compartmentalization regions of the hydrogel networks. This work would accelerate the exploitation of new supramolecular materials with lifelike features, including compartmentalized architectures, self‐evolving capacity, and interactive behaviors.

title: Sub‐Second Ratiometric Fluorescence Imaging of Histamine Dynamics in Living Cells via a Supramolecular Probe
abstract: ABSTRACT Histamine (HA) is a critical neurotransmitter, yet its intracellular dysregulation remains difficult to monitor due to the slow kinetics and environmental sensitivity of traditional fluorescent probes. Herein, we report a supramolecular ratiometric probe engineered via the host–guest self‐assembly of cationic fluorophores with cucurbit[7]uril (CB[7]). By precisely modulating the cationic locus within the guests, we achieved a 2:1 (host:guest) stoichiometric complex ( CB[7] 2 ⊃GA‐1 ) that displays a distinct 60 nm bathochromic shift. Functioning via a competitive displacement mechanism, this probe demonstrates exceptional selectivity and an ultrafast response time of 0.96 s ( k obs = 3.56 s − 1 ). We successfully utilized this system to visualize real‐time HA fluctuations in living mast cells with sub‐second resolution. Notably, our imaging revealed a quantitative correlation between nigericin‐induced cytoplasmic HA elevation and mast cell rupture. These findings validate the probe's efficacy in tracking cellular inflammatory responses and highlight its potential as an early‐warning indicator for drug‐induced cytotoxicity. Consequently, this work offers a robust tool for dissecting HA‐related pathophysiology and establishes a generalizable design paradigm for the rapid, ratiometric sensing of biologically relevant analytes.

title: Healthcare Waste-Derived Pyrolytic Char as a Functional Porous Carbon Material for Electrochemical Sensing of Estriol
abstract: Abstract This study presents an integrated approach for the sustainable management of healthcare waste (HCW) through slow pyrolysis and the application of the resulting pyrolytic char (Pc) for electrochemical sensing of estriol (E3), an emerging contaminant, in environmental and pharmaceutical samples. Pc was produced by the pyrolysis of HCW at 400 °C and characterized by Brunauer–Emmett–Teller (BET) analysis, Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), Raman spectroscopy, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS). Pc exhibited a mesoporous structure with a specific surface area of 6.9 m² g⁻¹, a pore volume of 0.026 cm³ g⁻¹, and an average pore diameter of 14.44 nm. Morphological analysis revealed a heterogeneous surface with a composition dominated by carbon (61.3%), oxygen (23.6%), silicon (9.6%), and aluminum (5.5%). A new conductive ink formulation was developed by modifying a commercial carbon-based ink with HCW-derived Pc, aiming to fabricate advanced and portable screen-printed electrodes for electrochemical E3 sensing. Pc proportions ranging from 1% to 10% were investigated. The sensor exhibited a high sensitivity of 58.5 nA L µmol⁻¹ and achieved a detection limit of 47.1 nmol L⁻¹ over a linear concentration range from 1.0 to 216.0 µmol L⁻¹. Recovery assays were performed in tap water, lagoon water, and pharmaceutical cream samples, yielding recoveries between 97.7% and 105.4% without the need for any sample pretreatment. These findings demonstrate that HCW-derived Pc is a promising, efficient, and sustainable sensing material for steroidal hormones, providing an integrated approach to waste valorization and environmental protection.

title: Modular van der Waals MOSFETs through layer-by-layer chalcogen substitutions
abstract: In two-dimensional transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs), the local electrostatic field of the chalcogen p -orbitals dictates the crystal field splitting of the transition metal d -orbitals, stabilizing diverse electronic states from semiconducting and semimetallic to exotic topological phases. On-demand substitution of the lattice chalcogens is therefore an efficient route to tuning TMDC electronic phases. Here, we custom-molded van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures by layer-by-layer vapor-phase chalcogen substitution starting from p -type WSe 2 multilayers into which we locally inscribed insulating WO x , n -type WS 2 , and semimetallic WTe 2 . This spatially precise conversion seamlessly integrated distinct electronic phases, both vertically and laterally, into modular vdW semiconductor heterostructures that are otherwise inaccessible. As a demonstration, we integrated WO x /WSe 2 local gate stacks to build ultrascaled metal oxide–semiconductor field effect transistors (MOSFETs), achieving an unprecedented subthreshold swing at subnanometer equivalent oxide thickness.

title: Linear and Branched Alkanes Separation Through Conjugated‐Polymer‐Framework Membranes
abstract: ABSTRACT The separation of linear and branched alkanes is critically important for improving the research octane number (RON) and advancing the sustainable development of the petrochemical industry. However, owing to their nearly identical kinetic diameters and closely related physicochemical properties (e.g., solubility parameters and boiling points), membrane‐based liquid‐phase separation of such linear and branched alkanes remains highly challenging. An example is the n‐ heptane/ iso ‐octane pair, which exhibits minimal differences in molecular size and physicochemical properties but a dramatic difference in RON. Herein, we report a conjugated‐polymer‐framework (CPF) membrane that enables molecular‐level separation of linear and branched alkanes. The crystallized selective layer of CPF membrane features intrinsic sub‐nanometer pores of ∼5.5 and 8.4 Å. With ethanol as an assisting agent, the membrane achieves a separation factor of 5.24 for n ‐heptane/ iso ‐octane mixture, together with a total mixture permeance of 0.020 kg m −2 h −1 bar −1 . This pronounced selectivity stems from ethanol‐induced modulation of transmembrane transport, which selectively mitigates the transport barrier of linear alkanes while exerting negligible influence on their branched counterparts, thereby enhancing kinetic selectivity. Furthermore, the CPF membrane exhibits robust separation performance over extended operation and across a wide range of feed compositions and pressures, highlighting its robustness for linear/branched alkane separation.

title: Evidence of large-scale and room-temperature stair-stepped quantum spin Hall states in Bi4Br4
abstract: Abstract Topological insulators host exotic quantum phenomena such as the quantum spin Hall (QSH) effect, which enables dissipationless one-dimensional edge conduction. Realizing such states at room temperature and on a macroscopic scale is essential for energy-efficient electronics and quantum technologies, yet remains a fundamental challenge due to material limitations. Here, using microwave impedance microscopy, we directly visualize robust conductive channels persisting up to 300 K in α-Bi4Br4 nanowires. Their stability and scalability are likely enabled by a “stair-stepped” stacking configuration on the side facets, a multilayer geometry in which QSH edge states from individual layers remain spatially decoupled. This configuration circumvents the stringent alignment and layer-number constraints of previous proposals, allowing robust stair-stepped QSH (SS-QSH) conduction in structures several micrometers long and hundreds of nanometers high. Magnetic-field- and temperature-dependent measurements are consistent with the topological nature of these conductive channels, as further supported by our theoretical analysis. Crucially, the conductance peaks and bulk signals scale with nanowire height, verifying the stair-stepped origin. Our results are also successfully reproduced by finite-element analysis simulations. This work establishes α-Bi4Br4 as a practical platform for high-temperature topological electronics and demonstrates a generalizable stacking strategy for designing scalable QSH systems.

title: In Situ Interfacial Assembly of Dynamic Semi‐Interpenetrating Biopolymer Networks for Robust and Mechanically Adaptive Droplet Interfaces
abstract: ABSTRACT Mechanically robust yet rapidly adaptive interfacial films are difficult to construct from naturally derived polymers because of their limited structural programmability. Herein, we report an in situ stepwise interfacial assembly strategy that transforms β‐sheet‐rich silk fibroin (SF) and rhamnolipid‐modified chitosan (CS‐RL) into a strong, dynamic oil‐water interfacial network. The resulting interfacial film rapidly transforms from a spherical droplet geometry to distorted tubular shape within seconds without rupture, and exhibiting markedly enhanced dilational rheological properties. Abundant β‐sheet provides rigid hydrophobic nanodomains, while flexible SF chains and positively charged CS‐RL form a semi‐interpenetrating network through electrostatic attractions. Additionally, the hydrophobic interactions between β‐sheet domains and CS‐RL create load‐bearing reinforcing nodes and dynamic polymer junctions, enabling coherent network remodeling and efficient stress dissipation under deformation. This unique interfacial network contributes to stable interface and controllable interfacial releasing and transportation. Emulsions stabilized by this network remain stable after 15 months and show pH‐responsive drug release even under acidic conditions. The network also enables reversible transport of 200 nm nanoplastics across both oil‐water and oil‐oil interfaces. This work establishes a molecular‐topological design principle for creating strong, adaptive, and functional natural‐polymer interfacial films, offering broad opportunities for advanced soft matter systems with programmable properties.

title: Multifunctional submicron-scale porous water-foamed cementitious materials
abstract: Abstract Conventional cement-based materials face a fundamental trade-off between low density and high performance, owing to their limited ability to precisely control pore structure. We use ultrasound carbonation to tailor the water distribution and confinement within the flocculation structure, thereby directing product nucleation and growth, and ultimately yielding a multifunctional submicron-scale water-foamed cementitious material. The matrix exhibits a highly refined pore network, 96.8% of which is smaller than 200 nm. The specific compressive strength is 22.5 kN·m·kg −1 , representing an increase of up to 162% relative to a laboratory-prepared foamed concrete control. Simultaneously, the sound transmission loss increases by 131.8% and 107.0% at 2000 Hz and 4000 Hz, respectively, while cumulative CO 2 uptake reaches 7.11% per unit mass of cement after 28 days. The approach relies solely on cement and water as raw materials, reducing process complexity and showing potential for production.

title: Dual-End Interfacial Regulation via Phase-Transitioned BSA-Assisted Layer-by-Layer Assembly of Metal–Phenolic Networks for Antifouling and Antibacterial Coatings
abstract: Abstract Biofilm formation poses a persistent health risk, yet conventional antibacterial coatings offer limited resistance to the initial conditioning-film stage that precedes bacterial colonization. Herein, we report a phase-transitioned BSA (PTB)-assisted layer-by-layer strategy that constructs a sequence-controlled metal–phenolic network (MPN) coating with dual-end interfacial regulation. A bottom PTB layer serves as a versatile adhesive primer, anchoring the MPN core to chemically inert LDPE via hydrophobic and coordination interactions at the interface, while a top PTB capping layer suppresses nonspecific protein adsorption and early stage biofouling. Stepwise coating growth was confirmed spectroscopically and microscopically, with thickness and Cu-associated signal intensity increasing progressively with cycle number. Capping the MPN coating with a PTB layer markedly reduced protein adsorption and bacterial adhesion. Antibacterial activity scaled with MPN layer number, reaching near-complete eradication of E. coli and S. aureus for the 3-layer configuration. The PTB-primed architecture withstood acid, alkali, ethanol, and sonication treatments that readily delaminated the counterpart lacking the bottom PTB layer, demonstrating pronounced interfacial robustness. Moreover, the strategy translated seamlessly to glass and porous fabric without loss of structural and functional fidelity. These findings establish PTB as a versatile interfacial building block that bridges adhesion and antifouling, offering a substrate-independent platform for contamination-resistant coatings.

title: Cell-free reconstitution reveals synergistic stabilization of microtubule doublets by PACRG and FAP20
abstract: Abstract Ciliary microtubule doublets, consisting of an incomplete B-tubule on the surface of a complete A-microtubule, form the fundamental structural framework of motile and sensory cilia/flagella. Ciliary proteins PACRG and FAP20, which are essential for flagellar stability and function, localize to the junction between the A- and the B-tubule. However, their precise role in microtubule doublet assembly and dynamics remains unknown. Here, using a cell-free assay, TIRF-microscopy, and cryo-electron tomography, we demonstrate that in combination PACRG and FAP20 stabilize B-tubule dynamics and microtubule doublet architecture. We show that together these proteins localize to the B-tubules in distinct, high-density patches, which locally stabilize B-tubule by decreasing its depolymerization velocity and increasing its rescue frequency. Cryo-tomography of in vitro reconstructed microtubule doublets in presence of PACRG and FAP20 reveals reduced B-tubule curvature fluctuations, promoting a more rigid and aligned conformation. Altogether, our findings suggest that PACRG and FAP20 function synergistically to reinforce microtubule doublet stability, ensuring ciliary integrity and function.

title: A Conjugated Neodymium‐Based Metal−Organic Framework for Efficient Photocatalytic CO 2 Cycloaddition
abstract: The photocatalytic cycloaddition of CO 2 with epoxides offers a sustainable approach for CO 2 fixation and value‐added carbonate synthesis, yet developing well‐defined photocatalysts that integrate narrow bandgap, abundant active sites, and strong CO 2 enrichment ability remains challenging. Herein, a new conjugated metal−organic framework (MOF) using hexahydroxytriphenylene as linkers and hexanuclear [Nd 6 ( μ 6 ‐CO 3 )O 12 ] 8− as inorganic nodes is constructed. The obtained FDM‐154 possesses interconnected 13.6 Å pores and a surface area of 532 m 2 g −1 , enabling efficient CO 2 enrichment (28.5 cm 3 g −1 ). Furthermore, FDM‐154 features a narrow optical bandgap of 1.12 eV, which facilitates photogenerated charge separation under visible light. Additionally, the MOF backbone is decorated with dense photoactive organic linkers and Nd 3+ Lewis acid sites that serve as active centers to efficiently activate both CO 2 and epoxide substrates during the photocatalytic process. FDM‐154 photocatalyst achieves high yield for CO 2 cycloaddition with epichlorohydrin under mild conditions, resulting from the combined effect of its suitable band structure, accessible active sites, and pore confinement effect.

title: Signatures of Band-like Charge Carrier Transport in a Three-Dimensional Fe-HHTP Metal–Organic Framework
abstract: Abstract Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) offer exceptional structural and chemical tunability, and the emergence of electrically conductive variants creates new opportunities for functional optoelectronic materials. Here, we investigate charge transport in a three-dimensional (3D) Fe-HHTP MOF (or Fe-CAU-42), composed of hexahydroxytriphenylene (HHTP)-based supertetrahedral units and trimeric Fe(III) oxo cluster nodes arranged in a diamond structure. Temperature dependent Van der Pauw (vdP) electrical conductivity measurements reveal an Arrhenius-type thermally activated charge transport mechanism operating in pelletized samples. Terahertz time-domain spectroscopy is used to probe the frequency-resolved complex conductivity of the Fe-HHTP pellet. The THz conductivity spectra are well-described by the Drude–Smith model, indicating the presence of mobile charge carriers with band-like dynamics subject to backscattering and localization. Temperature-dependent conductivity analysis reveals that the increase in conductivity with temperature is governed primarily by changes in carrier density rather than by changes in scattering time (and hence mobility). DC conductivities ranging from 6.54 × 10–3 S cm–1 at 300 K to 1.22 × 10–3 S cm–1 at 77 K are extracted from modeling of the THz data, in excellent agreement with van der Pauw measurements. The combined results establish a transport picture in which charge motion is dominated by localized band-like charge carriers with thermally activated carrier density, providing direct insight into carrier dynamics in conductive 3D catecholate MOFs.

title: Phenothiazine-Functionalized Triazine-Based Covalent Organic Frameworks for Efficient Photocatalytic Organic Synthesis
abstract: Abstract In this work, we present a donor–acceptor molecular engineering strategy in which three electron-donating moieties including benzene, triphenylamine, and phenothiazine are condensed with electron-deficient triazine monomers via Schiff-base reaction to furnish three crystalline photocatalysts, denoted as COF-C, COF-N, and COF-NS. Combined PXRD, FT-IR, and solid-state NMR analyses confirm the formation of all three COFs with eclipsed AA-stacked crystalline frameworks. Photophysical and photoelectrochemical measurements reveal that phenothiazine-functionalized COF-NS, bearing dual N and S heteroatoms, possesses the narrowest DFT-calculated HOMO–LUMO gap of 1.92 eV (together with an experimental optical band gap of 2.0 eV) and the broadest visible-light absorption range, thereby efficiently suppressing the recombination of photogenerated electron–hole pairs and delivering the optimal charge transport performance. The oxidative cyclization of o-phenylenediamine with benzaldehyde to 2-phenylbenzimidazole was selected as the model photocatalytic reaction. The catalytic activity follows the order COF-C &lt; COF-N &lt; COF-NS: under optimized conditions COF-NS affords a yield as high as 94%, accompanied by broad substrate compatibility, reliable gram-scale preparation, and excellent cycling stability. Reactive oxygen species trapping and EPR experiments identify superoxide radical anions, together with photogenerated electrons and holes, as the principal active species, from which a complete catalytic pathway was proposed. DFT calculations further demonstrate that the push–pull electronic system constructed between phenothiazine and triazine broadens the surface electrostatic potential and enhances charge separation efficiency, accounting at the electronic level for the superior performance of COF-NS. Overall, this study offers a rational strategy for the molecular design of high-performance COF photocatalysts and the green synthesis of nitrogen-containing heterocycles.

title: Naphthalenedisulfonic Acid-Regulated Ionic HOFs Enabling Single-Crystal Superprotonic Conductivity
abstract: Abstract Designing ionic hydrogen-bonded organic frameworks (iHOFs) with single-crystal superprotonic conductivity is of great significance for unraveling the mechanisms of proton-conductive materials at the molecular level. To regulate proton transport pathways, we synthesized two novel ionic hydrogen-bonded organic frameworks, iHOF-60 and iHOF-61, by adjusting the spatial configuration of the sulfonate groups. Both materials exhibit three-dimensional hydrogen-bonding networks and highly anisotropic proton conductivity, and clear proton transport pathways were identified through single-crystal structure analysis. Notably, experimental results show that iHOF-60 achieves a proton conductivity of up to 0.216 S cm−1 along the a-axis at 80 °C and 85% relative humidity, demonstrating exceptional superprotonic conduction performance. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations further confirm that iHOF-60 possesses superior proton transport properties compared to iHOF-61, which is attributable to its more continuous hydrogen-bonding network, smoother proton-transport pathway, and lower steric hindrance. These findings provide new experimental and theoretical insights for the design of high-performance proton-conducting materials.

title: Securing the Future: Porous Materials in Sensors for National Defense
abstract: Abstract Engineered porous materials such as metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) offer highly tunable, unique characteristics useful for durable, low power, selective gas sensors. This Perspective describes how MOF-based porous materials fit into the quickly emerging gas sensor landscape for national defense applications, and how they are anticipated to play an increasingly important role in the future to ensure national security. Herein is described in detail the relationships between the ability to judicious select porous materials to adsorb targeted key gases and the unique electrical responses for high consequence sensing related applications. Included are the materials strengths and limitations, followed by future materials needs and application growth areas. Finally, the emerging uses of AI/ML for materials and response design are highlighted. Altogether, porous materials such as MOFs offer outstanding chemical selectivity that can be leveraged for enhanced sensing in defense applications, providing better understanding of not only materials aging, but also chemical biological, radiological and nuclear threats.

title: Synthesis of Bi 2 Se 3 Nanosheets on COF Surfaces as Cathode for Lithium‐Sulfur Batteries: Synergistic Mechanism of Anchoring and Catalyzing Polysulfides
abstract: Lithium‐sulfur (Li‐S) batteries are one of the popular choices for the high energy storage systems due to their high theoretical energy density, cheap raw materials, and environmental friendliness. This work adopts a hydrothermal method to prepare covalent organic frameworks (COFs). Bi 2 Se 3 nanosheets are synthesized on COFs to obtain Bi 2 Se 3 /COFs composites serving as sulfur hosts. The porous COFs accommodate active sulfur and restrain the diffusion and migration of lithium polysulfides simultaneously. Furthermore, polar Bi 2 Se 3 immobilizes lithium polysulfides via chemical adsorption and efficiently alleviates the shuttle effect. Its layered nanostructure not only improves the structural stability of the cathode, but also endows the composites with superior electrical conductivity to accelerate the the redox reaction of sulfur. The results illustrate that the S/Bi 2 Se 3 /COFs electrode shows a remarkable initial discharge specific capacity of 961.2 mAh g −1 at 0.5 C. After 700 cycles, the capacity decay rate is 0.047% per cycle, showing excellent cycle stability. Therefore, the Bi 2 Se 3 /COFs are a desirable sulfur‐loading host for high‐performance Li‐S batteries.

title: Adaptive Interfacial Recognition Through Proton‐Coupled Force Reconfiguration in MOF@COF Composites
abstract: ABSTRACT Achieving dynamic, in situ switchable molecular recognition in porous composites remains challenging due to the difficulty of precisely modulating interfacial noncovalent interactions at the atomic level. Here, we demonstrated that proton‐coupled interfacial force reconstruction served as a general and efficient regulatory strategy to control adsorption‐desorption behaviors in a metal‐organic framework (MOFs)‐based covalent organic framework (COF) composite, NH 2 ‐UiO‐66@COF‐TpDBA (NU@FC). Reversible protonation‐deprotonation at carboxyl sites induced precise redistribution of the interfacial noncovalent force field, thereby endowing switchable molecular capture and markedly improving the utilization efficiency of interfacial active sites, constructing a stimuli‐responsive adsorption platform featuring molecular capture and release. This atomic‐scale regulation, coupled with solvent‐ triggered microenvironment modulation, allowed adaptive recognition of polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs) under diverse environments. Combined with the mechanically reinforced sheath‐tube‐protected solid‐phase microextraction device (STP‐SPME), this proton‐responsive interfacial regulation strategy was extended to an in situ, low‐cost, anti‐interference sample pretreatment system, achieving reliable identification and efficient extraction of trace organic pollutants from complex environmental matrices. Beyond device‐level performance, this study established proton‐coupled force reconstruction as a general design principle for constructing intelligently responsive MOF‐COF composites, bridging atomic‐scale interfacial modulation with expansive environmental analysis.

title: Synergistic Catalysis in Defect‐Engineered Zn‐MOF‐74‐Based Porous Liquids for Enhanced CO 2 Cycloaddition Under Mild Conditions
abstract: ABSTRACT Porous liquids (PLs), which combine permanent porosity with fluidity, represent an emerging class of materials with broad application prospects. The incorporation of catalytic sites into both the porous framework and the liquid medium further enables their use in catalysis. Here, we report a type III porous liquid (PL‐Zn‐MOF‐74‐DF) fabricated from a functional imidazolium‐based ionic liquid (IL1) and defective Zn‐MOF‐74‐DF, which exhibits enhanced CO 2 capture capacity and superior performance in the cycloaddition of CO 2 to epoxides compared to IL1 alone. Under mild conditions (50°C, 1 bar), the designed porous liquid boosts the conversion of styrene oxide (SO) by up to 22.6% and that of propylene oxide (PO) by 29.9%. Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations reveal that the remarkable catalytic enhancement stems from the synergistic interplay between IL1 and the defective metal sites in Zn‐MOF‐74‐DF, which facilitates CO 2 activation and stabilizes key reaction intermediates. This work provides both experimental and theoretical insights into the catalytic mechanism of porous liquids, paving the way for their rational design in sustainable catalysis.

It rejects visual regularity, local success, and post-selected demonstrations as evidence of mass manufacturing. The central observable is the unselected joint distribution of structure, material state, correction history, release survival, and function. Central deliverable The final reconstructable object is the Wafer Assembly Field. It binds template grammar, component and material identity, local interaction rules, transport and field history, defect ontology, correction actions, terminal function, sorting and lifecycle costs, negative evidence, and successor authority. Another team must be able to reproduce, refute, repair, fork, or retire the route.

title: Electrochemical strategies for peptide synthesis, deprotection and scalable reactor technologies
abstract: Peptides have high target specificity, favourable safety profiles, and increasing applications in oncology, metabolic disorders, infectious diseases, and precision medicine, making them one of the fastest-growing classes of therapeutic molecules. Traditional peptide synthesis involves more hazardous solvents and stoichiometric quantities of coupling reagents, which lead to high process mass intensity and environmental impact. In electrochemical synthesis, electrons are traceless redox reagents that allow for the controlled activation and transformation of peptide substrates under mild conditions. Advances in electrochemical peptide bond formation, electrochemical deprotection methods, and new technologies of electrochemical reactors for peptide synthesis are critically discussed. The focus is on phosphine-mediated anodic peptide coupling, iodide-mediated amide formation, residue-selective electrochemical modifications and redox-triggered deprotection methods. Advances in flow electrochemistry, scalable reactor designs and sustainable peptide production methods are thoroughly discussed. The effect of electrochemical parameters such as the electrode materials, current density, solvent systems, electrolytes, reaction time, and reactor design on reaction efficiency and selectivity is critically evaluated. However, there are still some issues that need to be addressed, such as the scope of the substrates, the lack of understanding of the mechanisms, fouling of the electrodes, scalability and the absence of a standardized method of reporting. Opportunities for the future include the combination of electro­chemistry and continuous-flow processing, sustainable solvent systems, automated synthesis platforms, and machine learning-assisted process optimization. Electrochemical approaches provide valuable potential for development of greener, more efficient and potentially scalable technology for next-generation pharmaceutical manufacturing of peptides.

title: Protein Self-Assembly as a Design Principle for Enzyme Immobilisation in Biocatalysis
abstract: Enzyme immobilisation is essential for translating biocatalytic processes from the laboratory to industrial applications by improving enzyme stability, recovery, and reuse. It underpins sustainable processes in pharmaceuticals, biofuels, and food production, but conventional immobilisation strategies involve inherent trade-offs. Covalent attachment prevents enzyme leaching but may distort the active site, whereas physical adsorption better preserves enzyme conformation but allows enzyme leaching. Furthermore, carrier-based methods frequently encounter mass-transfer limitations and may require external cross-linkers, hindering broader industrial application. Recent advances in synthetic biology and materials science have accelerated the development of protein-based materials for biocatalysis. This review examines protein self-assembly as a unifying design principle for enzyme immobilisation, enabling programmable assembly under relatively mild conditions to overcome key limitations of conventional strategies. We discuss naturally derived structures such as bacterial microcompartments and engineered systems including virus-like particles, elastin-like polypeptides, and SpyTag/SpyCatcher, which support programmable enzyme organisation and enable compartmentalised multi-enzyme cascade reactions. Building on this, a major focus is placed on catalytically active inclusion bodies (CatIBs). As robust, intrinsically self-immobilised protein aggregates, CatIBs represent a simplified, carrier-free platform offering potential process and cost advantages for industrial biocatalysis.

title: Unleashing Platinum‐Sulfur Synergy in Ultranano‐Structured Conjugated Porous Polymers Based on Thiazole for Efficient Hydrogen Generation
abstract: ABSTRACT The molecular design of conjugated porous polymers (CPPs) offers a powerful strategy to control their optoelectronic properties and interactions with semiconductor and metallic cocatalyst interfaces. Here, we develop an ultrananostructured thiazolo[5,4‐d]thiazole (TzTz)‐based CPP (UN_IEP‐48), whose sulfur‐containing units provide favourable sites for interaction with Pt. High‐performance microfluidic processing enables its intimate integration with TiO 2 , yielding an optimized UN_IEP‐48@T3 hybrid containing only 3 wt.% polymer. Photoluminescence and transient absorption spectroscopy reveal efficient charge separation consistent with a direct Z‐scheme mechanism, directing the reduction pathway toward the CPP. Remarkably, photodeposition of only 0.5 wt.% Pt increases the H 2 evolution rate from 3.0 to 94.3 mmol g −1 h −1 , corresponding to a 30‐fold enhancement and a photonic efficiency of 34.91%. Increasing Pt loading to 1 wt.% provides essentially no further improvement, highlighting efficient noble‐metal utilization. Microscopy reveals preferential Pt localization on polymer‐rich regions, while FTIR, XPS, and electrochemical impedance measurements support strong Pt–TzTz interactions and facilitated electron transfer. These results demonstrate how molecular engineering of CPPs can couple nanoscale heterojunction formation with cocatalyst interfacial chemistry, maximizing photocatalytic H 2 production while minimizing noble‐metal loading.

title: Chemoselective Electrochemical Synthesis of 3-Hydroxyisoindolinones from Phthalimide Imines
abstract: Abstract We report an electrochemical method for the radical–radical coupling of alkyl iodides with phthalimide imines under mild conditions. This operationally simple electro-reductive procedure enables selective reduction of carbonyl groups, offering an efficient route to access functionalized 3-hydroxyisoindolinones in moderate-to-excellent yields. Notably, the highly functionalized 3-hydroxyisoindolinones have shown promising bioactivity in preliminary assessments, pointing to the significant potential of this chemical scaffold for anticancer cell applications. A comparative analysis has demonstrated that the hydrazone moiety within the product structure plays an indispensable role in conferring bioactivity.

title: Electrolyte- and Catalyst-Free Electrochemical Synthesis of Unsymmetrical Diorganoyl Selenides
abstract: Abstract A facile electrocatalytic radical coupling of Katritzky salts with diselenides for the efficient synthesis of various alkyl aryl unsymmetrical selenides has been developed under mild conditions. This sustainable protocol is driven by renewable electrical energy, features a broad substrate scope, good functional group tolerance, and practical scalability. The reaction proceeds without the need for any external electrolyte, catalyst, or metal, in accordance with green chemistry principles.

title: Decoupling the Conductivity–Seebeck Trade‐Off in N‐Type MXene/Conjugated Polyelectrolyte Thermoelectric Bilayers
abstract: ABSTRACT To decouple the Seebeck coefficient from electrical conductivity in metallic thermoelectric (TE) systems, we investigated bilayer heterostructures of MXene (Ti 3 C 2 T x ) and conjugated polymers with anionic (–SO 3– Na + , CPE‐Na), neutral (CP), and cationic (–N + (CH 3 ) 3 Br–, CPE‐Br) side chains. Strong electrostatic anchoring between the cationic ammonium side chains and electronegative MXene terminations induces a previously unreported Coulombic trap‐induced filtering mechanism, distinct from conventional energy filtering. The resulting localized potential wells selectively trap low‐energy carriers to enhance the Seebeck coefficient, while concurrent lattice stiffening suppresses electron–phonon scattering and preserves high‐energy carrier transport. This decoupling raises Hall mobility from 1.01 to 5.40 cm 2 V −1 s −1 and the Seebeck coefficient from –8.6 to –19.0 µV K −1 while maintaining a metallic conductivity of 5291.9 S cm −1 . The optimized MXene/CPE‐Br film, processed with a halogen‐free solvent, achieves a record power factor of 190.5 µW m −1 K −2 and a peak figure of merit ( zT ) of 0.0279. Strong interfacial adhesion further imparts good electromechanical durability under repeated bending to a flexible TE generator, providing an effective strategy to address the transport limitations of n‐type MXene‐based TE materials.

title: Mixed-Lignin Precursor Engineering for Hierarchically Porous Pseudo-Graphitic Carbon Toward High-Performance Supercapacitors
abstract: Developing biomass-derived carbon electrodes with simultaneously optimized pore architecture, graphitic ordering, and surface chemistry remains a challenge for high-performance supercapacitors. Herein, a dual-lignin precursor engineering strategy based on lignosulfonate and alkaline lignin is proposed to construct hierarchically porous carbons via an ex situ method. Benefiting from the complementary characteristics and cooperative interactions of the two lignins, the optimized carbon exhibits a well-balanced porous architecture composed of interconnected carbon nanosheets with predominantly pseudo-graphitic domains accompanied by locally graphitized regions. The mixed-lignin strategy effectively regulates sulfur retention and removal during carbonization, while the coexistence of oxygen- and sulfur-containing functional groups may improve electrode wettability and contribute to charge storage, thereby favoring substantial outer-surface charge accessibility with contributions from other charge-storage processes. Among all samples, the optimized 2L1A electrode delivers a high specific capacitance of 386.7 F g−1 at 1 A g−1 in a three-electrode configuration. The assembled symmetric supercapacitor delivers an energy density of 40.4 Wh kg−1 together with 97.4% capacitance retention after 10,000 charge–discharge cycles. Comprehensive kinetic analyses further demonstrate rapid electron/ion transport, predominant surface-controlled charge storage, and excellent reversibility. This work demonstrates the potential of mixed-lignin precursor engineering for the rational design of high-performance carbon electrodes for advanced supercapacitors.
